newsitem.title: UK: Stg pushes UK export orders to five year low-BCC.
newsitem.headline: Stg pushes UK export orders to five year low-BCC.

text.p: British exporters are facing their toughest summer in five years with the super strong pound set to heap further pressure on manufacturers, the British Chambers of Commerce said on Wednesday.
The BCC's second quarter survey, which canvassed more than 9,000 companies, found that overseas orders for both manufacturing and service sector firms have dropped to levels last seen in 1992.
Export sales for manufacturers have fallen for the fifth consecutive quarter to 1993 levels.
"This survey paints a gloomy picture for exporters particularly in the smaller business sector," said Ian Peters, deputy director-general of the BCC.
"With interest rates set to increase further, our concern is that sterling will continue to strengthen causing significant damage to the UK's international competitiveness."

The BCC said export sales to the service sector have also fallen to a two-year low but service companies have been benefiting from buoyant domestic demand with sales, investment and employment indicators at or near record levels.
Manufacturers, on the other hand, are having their exports suffocated by the stronger pound and do not seem to be benefiting from the full force of domestic demand.
That raises a dilemma for policy makers, the BCC said, adding that its preferred solution was for personal tax rises in the budget.
"Whilst inflation is the greater threat, the Bank of England must be ever sensitive to the effect that further rate increases will have on British exporters and manufacturers."
